feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+8?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/1adec10c20862d7015466efc5ded1e966e959ac3f6141163afa26802b502d49e.png)

 

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/9651fab70ad189764143d92f89938cff1293a390bfca693c567bb33220ff859e.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $8$ units up to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}+8.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(0,7)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from from $y=0$ to $y=8.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/1d41ded0d251b46ad6f137b6686e31bfdad299c62a1496e0782ada5d400780bf.png)
